Portfolio Execution — Complete Before Moving On
This opened because you had a real conversation with an active relationship. Complete the RM playbook questions now so the relationship has a clear health signal, growth opportunity and next move. Use what naturally came up in the conversation. If a topic truly was not discussed, choose Not discussed today rather than guessing. Then save the touch and portfolio together.
WHEN THIS POPS UP
A real live conversation with an Amanda-owned active partner triggers Portfolio Execution. Finish it before moving to the next person.
It does NOT pop up for: cold calls, no answer, voicemail-only, birthday/holiday touches, or routine admin.
Goal: know what is happening in the business, what they need, whether business is leaking, how supported they feel, and exactly what we do next.
RM PLAYBOOK · COVER THESE ON THE CONVERSATION.
1. Business: “What are you focused on right now / what’s coming up?”
2. Support: “Anything making business harder or anything we could do better?”
3. Opportunity / leakage: “Are we getting most of your lending opportunities, or are some going elsewhere?”
4. Growth + next move: “What’s the best next move for us to help you?”
If something genuinely did not come up, choose “Not discussed today.” Do not guess or force the question. The tracker keeps existing portfolio information.

Activity Guide
The role comes down to two things: bring in new agents, and keep the agents we have engaged and getting value from us. Every activity type below fits into one of those two buckets. Use this anytime you're not sure what to log something as.
If you're mid-call and not sure which type fits, log your best guess and keep going, don't stop the conversation to check this guide. You can always fix it after: open Activity Feed, find the entry, hit Edit.
Quick note on "Agent Talk-to's" Every touch should leave the agent with something of value: a market insight, useful feedback, a resource, a pipeline review, a file update, a genuine check-in on how their business is going. Think account executive: proactive, consultative, and always bringing something of value. It's what keeps you top-of-mind so agents think of NFM first.
1 · New Business (Growth) 🌱
Agents you've never worked with before. These don't count toward your Talk-to goal; they've got their own goals to hit.
Cold CallsYour very first reach-out to someone new, not in the book yet. If you've talked to them before, even once, it's not cold anymore.
New Realtor MeetingThe first real sit-down is structured and 20–40 minutes max. Book it in-office or as a focused coffee meeting — never lunch. In-office: give the office tour and introduce the team. Set the agenda, learn and document their Top 3 lending-partner needs, ask what a lender has done in the past that hurt the experience, tie our Standards of Service back to what matters to them, confirm contact information, and ask directly for the next buyer opportunity. Lunches are for established Channel/A/B relationships and break breads.
2 · Get the Opportunity 🚀
That first meeting isn't the finish line; they're not really on board until they send us a lead. Getting them set up on the tools is what makes that first lead possible, so keep following up until it happens.
New Agent Follow-up counts as Talk-toChecking in and helping a newly met agent get set up on HomeBot, ListReports, and Total Expert, moving them toward that first lead.
Onboarding checklistThe 7 quick tasks (Retained Report, Sa Team email, HomeBot, ListReports, Total Expert, group text, asking for the opportunity + referral language + LP CC'd). Complete these the same day as the meeting.
Gifting campaignEvery agent in this program needs a call once a week for their first 4 weeks. This is one of the most important parts of the role. Tracked on Snapshot, which follows the 4-Week Conversion Skillset: break the ice, a value touch, an opportunity call, then accountability follow-up.
3 · If They Go Quiet: Reconnect 🔁
If an agent hasn't sent us a lead in 90 days, they fall off and land on the Reconnect list (its own tab). That's a flag that it's time to work on earning a lead from them again. Re-engaging someone from that list is not a Cold Call: the relationship already exists, you're just picking it back up. Log it as Reconnect Outreach, not a regular Agent Talk-to, since technically they're not active until they send a lead again. It still counts toward your Talk-to goal.
4 · Staying in Touch 💛
Everything marked counts as Talk-to feeds into your weekly Talk-to goal (100/week). Log it once and it does double duty. Whatever the reason for the touch, use it to get real feedback on how the relationship is going. Every touch is an opportunity.
Agent Talk-to counts as Talk-toA proactive check-in with an agent who's currently active and sending business.
Reconnect Outreach counts as Talk-toThe right type for re-engaging someone from the Reconnect list. It's not a Cold Call since you already know them, but a regular Agent Talk-to isn't quite right either since they haven't sent a lead in 90+ days.
CTC Call counts as Talk-toProcess: call the agent, leave a voicemail if no answer, then follow up with a text. Script is in Scripts + Training. Get feedback from both the buyer's agent and the listing agent. Share that feedback on WhatsApp with the team in real-time, proactively, the way Daniel does, proactively. Check Encompass for the CTC milestone Always ask the listing agent for a meeting if they don't already work with us; a closing is a natural door-opener. If there's a closing issue or poor feedback, set the outcome to "Needs manager attention" so it surfaces for the team.
Under Contract Call counts as Talk-to, note requiredFirst call to the listing agent as soon as a deal you're the buyer's lender on goes under contract. Script is in Scripts + Training.
Birthday / Holiday Outreach counts as Talk-toA personal touch: wish the agent a happy birthday or happy holidays. When the birthday alert shows on Snapshot, send a text, give a quick call, or both. If the agent is a top producer, let the team know so they can wish them well too. When you are on a call with any agent, check if their birthday is on file — a lot of data is missing. If you do not have it, ask and add it to their contact so you never miss it.
Agent Appreciation counts as Talk-toRecognizing a top producer or celebrating a milestone.
Market Update counts as Talk-toSharing what's happening in the market: inventory, days on market, buyer demand, listing trends. This isn't financing or rates; that stays with the LP team.
Break Breads note required, 10+ wordsMore than a meal: sitting down with the agent to get real feedback and confirm the relationship is genuinely solid. Its own goal (5/week), separate from Talk-to's. To figure out who's due, check the Break Bread Due List on Snapshot (or the Face Time Tracker on the LP tracker), it shows last touch date per agent across both you and the LPs. Consider bringing the assigned LP along when it makes sense.
Realtor Buddy Referral AskAsk an existing happy agent to introduce you to someone else they know. Log the ask when you make it; do not create a follow-up obligation for that agent. Outcome goal: 3 actual buddy introductions received per week. When an intro arrives, use “Buddy intro received” so the tracker records the result separately from the ask.
Co-hosted EventHosting something together with the agent.
Team / Office PresentationA presentation or relationship meeting with a Realtor team, brokerage, builder office, or partner group. Count the event once as one partner meeting regardless of how many people attend; it does not count as multiple New Realtor Meetings.
Still not sure? Just ask.
Agent Strategy
Skillset Training: talking points and frameworks for actual agent conversations.
The How to Refer System
Don't just ask for leads. Install the referral language. The agent needs the exact text, email path, and buyer expectations, not a vague ask.
Agent uses the exact script at the first buyer interaction → Buyer expects a lender call within hours → Lender receives name, phone, email, goals, timing, and obstacles.
Coach this line after sending the guide: "This is the exact language I recommend using whenever a buyer mentions they may purchase."
Coach Agents to Refer Earlier
Earlier introductions create more control and more conversion. Don't wait until the buyer is ready to tour homes.
Early = plan + education + excitement + lender preference
Late = rate comparison + urgency + weaker influence
Existing Partner Lead Growth Framework
Earn more share by tying support to the agent's goals. The ask doesn't feel like begging when it follows value, feedback, and accountability.
1. State the goal"I want to earn all of your business."
2. Ask for feedback"What can I improve to earn more?"
3. Learn their goalsTransactions, pipeline, stuck buyers.
4. Offer a specific actionReview stalled buyers, events, intros.
5. Ask for greater opportunityEarlier intros, larger lead share.
Core question: "What can I improve to earn more of your business?"
Relationship Builder vs. Transactional Lender
Deep relationships reduce partner turnover. Business relationships are replaceable; personal loyalty is harder to displace.
Transactional lender: calls only when there's a deal, sends generic marketing, asks for leads, disappears after closing.
Relationship builder: builds a personal cadence, creates value, helps the agent hit goals, puts the agent first.
Relationship actions: relevant humor, family milestones, events with partners, agent introductions.
Portfolio Details
Partner Health — What It Means
Partner Health is now an action signal, not just a report. Red and Yellow partners feed the daily Workflow so the portfolio gets worked before relationships quietly slip.
Green
Relationship is on cadence, recent business is healthy, and there is no active competitor-risk flag. Maintain the normal relationship plan.
Yellow
A warning signal: business or meaningful contact is getting stale. Reconnect, identify what changed, document the next growth move, and schedule the next meaningful touch.
Red
Needs action now: major lapse in business/contact cadence or competitor risk. Make a meaningful relationship move, document what is happening, and escalate when needed.
Daily priority: urgent escalation → must-do transaction calls → Partner Health DO FIRST → due reconnects / follow-ups → new-meeting push → Partner Health maintenance. Health stays core work; low-signal stale relationships simply do not outrank stronger opportunities.
Today's task vs. health status: once you log a relationship-work attempt today, that person comes off Today's Partner Health work list immediately — even if you only reached voicemail/no answer. Their underlying Red/Yellow health can remain until a meaningful live connection or business signal actually improves it. This prevents duplicate work without falsely turning the relationship Green.
Health is calculated from recent lead activity, meaningful relationship contact, tier cadence, and competitor-risk signals. A partner who sent a lead within the last 14 days is suppressed from Today’s Partner Health work list because that lead is current engagement; an explicit competitor-risk flag can still keep them actionable. Click any Partner Health tile in Portfolio Review to see the actual names.
Remove from Amanda’s prospect call list
This keeps the person in the database, removes them from Amanda’s prospecting list, and automatically pulls the next eligible prospect so her call target does not shrink.
Keep active + note only: listing-heavy / mostly sellers, low production, part-time, or temporarily slow. Those can still become buyer/referral opportunities and should not be excluded automatically.
Amanda’s RM Scripts + Playbooks
Use one guide at a time. Follow it. Log the outcome. Move to the next priority.
1 · Book a New Realtor MeetingCold call → pushback → meeting booked＋

WHEN DO I USE THIS?

Use this for a Realtor you have never spoken with before. If you have already spoken with them, do not log a Cold Call.

BEFORE YOU CALL

  1. Look up the agent.
  2. Find one real detail: recent listing, sale, office, team, or market.
  3. Know the goal: book a 20-minute first meeting.

WHAT DO I SAY?

“Hi [Name], this is Amanda with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I wanted to introduce myself. We work with agents on buyer financing strategy, communication and smooth closings. I’d like to learn more about your business and show you how our team works. Can we meet for 20 minutes next week?”

BOOK IT

“I have Tuesday at 11:00 or Thursday at 2:00. Which works better?”

NO ANSWER

Leave one voicemail. Send the follow-up text. Set the next attempt. Do not leave the task unfinished.

DONE =

The meeting is booked OR the next outreach date is set and logged.

2 · Run the First Realtor Meeting20–40 minutes · office or structured coffee · no lunch＋
FIRST MEETING RULE: 20–40 minutes max. Book it in the office or as a structured coffee. Do not book lunch for a first meeting.

1. SET THE AGENDA

“My goal today is simple. I want to learn about your business and what you need from a lending partner. Then I’ll show you how our team works and how we support our agents and buyers. At the end, we’ll decide if it makes sense to work together.”

2. IF THEY COME TO THE OFFICE

Give the office tour. Introduce the team. Then sit down and start the meeting.

3. ASK THE TOP 3 QUESTIONS

  1. “Where have most of your last 20 clients come from?”
  2. “What are the top 3 things you need from a lending partner?”
  3. “What has a lender done in the past that hurt a deal, created stress, or made you look bad?”

Write down the answers. Do not rely on memory.

4. TIE OUR STANDARDS TO THEIR TOP 3

Show how our communication, pre-approval process and on-time closing standards solve the exact things they told you matter.

5. ASK FOR THE OPPORTUNITY

“Based on what you shared, I’m confident our team can deliver on the things that matter most to you. Send us your next buyer and give us the chance to show you.”

6. BEFORE YOU LEAVE

  1. Confirm phone.
  2. Confirm email.
  3. Get mailing address.
  4. Confirm the next follow-up.
  5. Complete the same-day onboarding checklist in the tracker.

DONE =

Top 3 documented + Standards reviewed + contact info confirmed + opportunity asked + next step logged.

3 · Follow Up · Weeks 1–4Required weekly conversion cadence＋
NON-NEGOTIABLE: Every New Realtor Meeting gets one conversion touch every week for 4 weeks. Log each week separately.

WEEK 1 · BREAK THE ICE

Call. Reinforce that you are excited to work together. Ask if anything has come up that we can help with.

WEEK 2 · ADD VALUE

Call with a useful reason: buyer scenario, market/payment idea, listing support, team resource, or another real value touch.

WEEK 3 · ASK FOR THE OPPORTUNITY

“I wanted to check in and ask directly: do you have a buyer right now that we can help you with?”

WEEK 4 · ACCOUNTABILITY FOLLOW-UP

Call. Reference the relationship and the first meeting. Ask what is keeping us from getting the first opportunity. Get a clear next step.

DONE =

Week 1, Week 2, Week 3 and Week 4 each show completed in Today. A random Talk-to does not close the weekly task.

4 · Work Existing PartnersRetain the relationship and create the next opportunity＋

WHEN DO I USE THIS?

Use this for an active relationship that needs a follow-up, Face Time, feedback call, growth conversation, or next move.

CALL WITH A PURPOSE

  1. Know why you are calling before you dial.
  2. Ask how the relationship is going.
  3. Ask what is working.
  4. Ask what needs to improve.
  5. Ask about current buyers, listings, pipeline or another opportunity.
  6. Set the next move before ending the call.

TIME RULE

Channel / A / B get priority relationship time. Lunches, Face Time and longer meetings belong here when they support retention or growth.

DONE =

Outcome logged + next relationship move documented.

5 · Grow C → BDevelop Amanda-owned C relationships＋

GOAL

Turn a C relationship into repeat business. Do not spend Channel/A/B-level time on routine C maintenance.

WHAT DO I DO?

  1. Look for real evidence: recent lead, closing, engagement, stated opportunity, or strong growth signal.
  2. Call with a specific growth reason.
  3. Ask for the next buyer or business opportunity.
  4. Document what would move the relationship forward.
  5. When the evidence is strong, click Send to Nyny for Review.

TIME RULE

C agents get efficient touches. Use a call, short meeting, office meeting or quick coffee. Do not book lunch unless the relationship has a documented growth reason and has earned more time.

DONE =

Next move documented OR strong candidate sent to Nyny.

6 · Reconnect an AgentRestart a relationship that went quiet＋

THIS IS NOT A COLD CALL

You already know this person. Log it as Reconnect Outreach.

WHAT DO I SAY?

“Hi [Name], I wanted to reconnect. It’s been a little while since we worked together and I wanted to check in, hear what you’re working on, and see where our team can help.”

ASK FOR A REAL NEXT STEP

Ask about current buyers, listings, pipeline, a meeting, or a specific way the team can help. Do not end with “let me know.”

DONE =

Reconnect logged + next step set.

7 · Transaction CallsNew Contract + CTC · buyer + listing agent scripts＋
WHY THIS MATTERS
A listing agent on one of our live transactions is the warmest new relationship available: there is already a deal, a reason to call, and multiple chances to demonstrate how we work. Do not wait until after closing to ask for the meeting.

BEFORE THE NEW CONTRACT CALL

  1. Check Power BI / Active Agent Search first. If the listing agent already works with an NFM loan officer, protect that relationship. Represent NFM well and do not pursue them as a new retained relationship.
  2. Have the buyer name, subject property, buyer agent and listing agent contact information in front of you.
  3. If there is a transaction coordinator, ask who needs updates. Do not add extra file data to the tracker just to store it.

NEW CONTRACT · BUYER AGENT

“Hi [Agent], it’s Amanda with the Daniel Sa Team. Congratulations on getting [Buyer] under contract on [Property]. I wanted to reach out personally, make sure you know who to call on our side, and see if there is anything you want us watching closely as we move through the file.”

Then ask: What communication is most helpful for you? Any concern or timing issue we should know about? Is there anyone else on your team we should keep informed?

“Perfect. We’ll keep you updated and stay ahead of anything that could create stress. If anything comes up, call or text us directly.”

NEW CONTRACT · LISTING AGENT

“Hi [Agent], it’s Amanda with the Daniel Sa Team at NFM Lending. I’m calling because our buyer [Buyer] is under contract on your listing at [Property]. Congratulations. I wanted to introduce myself, give you a direct point of contact on the lending side, and make sure we understand what matters most to you on this transaction.”

Ask these discovery questions:

  1. Is the closing local, remote, or mail-away?
  2. How do you prefer we communicate with you?
  3. Which milestones do you specifically want a direct update on?
  4. Is there anything you are concerned about or want us watching closely?
  5. Is this a simultaneous closing for your seller?
  6. Who else on your team needs updates?

SET THE STANDARD

“Our goal is simple: close on time, communicate proactively, and make sure there are no surprises. If we miss something, I want you to tell me. If we deliver, I’m going to ask for a few minutes of your time because I’d love the opportunity to earn more business together.”

COMMITMENT CLOSE · ASK EARLY

“If we can deliver a smooth transaction and have the loan clear to close at least three days before closing, can I earn 15 minutes of your time to talk about how we might grow our businesses together?”

Do not wait until after funding. The meeting opportunity is earned during the transaction. Put the commitment on the table on the introductory call.

HIGH-LEVERAGE FOLLOW-UP MOMENTS

  1. Appraisal at value: call the listing agent directly with the good news when possible. Let them be the hero to their seller.
  2. Clear to Close: call the buyer agent and listing agent directly. Congratulate them, confirm the transaction is moving cleanly, get feedback, and collect the meeting commitment.

CTC · BUYER AGENT

“Great news — we are clear to close on [Buyer] at [Property]. I wanted you to hear it directly from us. How has the experience been from your side? Anything we could have done better or anything you want us to keep doing?”

CTC · LISTING AGENT

“Great news — we are clear to close on [Buyer] at [Property]. I wanted to call you directly so you can update your seller. How has the lending side felt from your perspective?”

If they do not already work with NFM and the experience has been positive, collect the commitment:

“We said we’d earn 15 minutes if we delivered. Let’s get that on the calendar while we’re here — what does next week look like?”

NO ANSWER / VOICEMAIL

Leave a voicemail that requests a callback, then send the required follow-up text. Do not mark the transaction call complete until the required text is documented.

DONE =

Required sides worked + outcome/feedback logged + issues escalated + listing-agent meeting opportunity intentionally asked when appropriate.

8 · Ask for Referrals + OpportunitiesAsk clearly. Get the introduction.＋

ASK FOR THE BUYER

“Do you have a buyer right now that we can help you with?”

ASK FOR THE INTRODUCTION

Use a group text first. Introduce the buyer and lending team in the same thread so the handoff is immediate and clear.

ASK FOR A REALTOR INTRODUCTION

“Who are 2 or 3 agents you respect that you think I should meet?”

DONE =

Make the opportunity or introduction OR schedule and log the next follow-up.

Your Role
Relationship Manager — Daniel Sa Team, NFM Lending
Responsible for growing the team's active agent count and keeping those relationships producing. An active agent is one who has sent us a lead — agents who haven't sent a lead within 90 days fall off the active list and move to the Reconnect queue. Two core responsibilities: bring in new agents through cold calling, outreach, and meetings; and retain the agents we have through consistent, value-driven contact, feedback, and follow-through so they keep referring their clients.
Working from home: The expectation is that you are actively working your full hours, on Teams, and responsive. If something comes up and you are not able to work, please take PTO or come into the office. WFH is a privilege and the standard is the same as being in office.

Encompass Cheat Guide
You don't need to know how to process a file. You need to know where to look when you're talking to an agent. Before every call, have three things open: RETR (to reference their recent sales), Encompass (to check file status), and the team inbox (to catch any recent updates).
Milestones — what each one means
StartedApplication has been taken. File is open and still with the sales team.
ProcessingFile is with the loan manager for review. Being prepared for submittal to underwriting.
SubmittalLoan has been submitted to underwriting for initial review.
ApprovalUnderwriting has reviewed and approved. There may still be conditions to satisfy — check the Conditions tab for what's outstanding.
ResubSubmitted to underwriting for final review. Normal and expected — doesn't mean something went wrong. If an agent asks why, tell them it's a standard step in the review process.
Clear to Close (CTC)All conditions met. Ready to schedule closing. Your trigger for a CTC call to both agents.
Received by CloserClosing docs are with the title/closing company. Closing is imminent.
Docs SigningClosing docs are out to title. Borrower is signing.
Conditions — what they mean
Prior to DocsClear these before sending closing docs. The file cannot move forward until you clear them.
Prior to FundingClear these before releasing funds. Closing can happen, but funds do not move until you finish them.
Rate lock
Find the lock status and expiration date in the loan file under Rate Lock or Pricing. If a lock is expiring soon and the file isn't close to closing, flag it to the LP. Rate conversations stay with the LP team.
Where to find things mid-call
Current milestonePipeline view — the status column next to the file. Check before every call.
Closing dateTop of the loan file in property and closing details. Check if it matches the contract date — if they don't align, mention it to the LP.
Outstanding conditionsConditions tab. Shows what's still needed and whether it's prior to docs or prior to funding.
Assigned LP / ProcessorFile summary under team members. If you need to escalate, this tells you who to go to.
Buyer infoBorrower summary tab — name, contact, employment, loan amount.
Rate lock statusRate Lock or Pricing section. Locked vs. floating, and expiration date.
Attend the weekly pipeline call every Tuesday at 10:30am. This is where you'll hear what's moving, what's stalled, and what agents may need a touch on. It's one of the best ways to stay ahead of conversations before agents call you.
If an agent asks something you can't answer with confidence, it's always fine to say "Let me look into that and get back to you shortly" — then actually follow up. Never guess on a file detail.
Resources
These tools exist to help you find answers quickly and show up prepared. The more you use them, the more confident you'll sound in the field.
RETRAgent and brokerage lookup — and your secret weapon before every cold call and reconnect. Pull up their profile before you dial: see their recent sales, current listings, and brokerage. Congratulating them on a specific recent sale ("I saw your listing at 123 Main just closed — congrats!") turns a cold call into a warm one instantly.
NFM ChatGPTGreat for drafting, quick explanations, and thinking through how to handle a conversation. Use it before, during, or after calls.
All RegsNFM's underwriting guidelines. A solid resource when you want to understand what's possible for a buyer before the conversation goes further.
EncompassFile status, milestones, conditions, closing dates. Have it open before agent calls. See the Encompass Cheat Guide for where to find specific things.
Team inboxHave it open and searchable before calls. If an agent asks about something specific on a file, you can pull the relevant email thread in real time in real time.
VelocifyCRM where leads are added and tracked. When an agent refers a buyer, this is where the lead lives. Have it open so you can see what's been referred and by whom.
The more familiar these tools become, the more confident you'll sound in the field. When you do need to bring something to the team, coming in with what you already found makes the conversation faster and makes the conversation more productive for everyone.
